title: Emergency: runtime 'mosaic' KV-index entropy causing tenant memory spikes and GPU OOMs
creator: Sana Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated environments reported sudden GPU OOMs correlated with large increases in per-tenant memory RSS. Investigation points to a runtime component we call the 'mosaic' KV-index -- an adaptive sharding/metadata layer used for high-throughput session prefix caching. Under certain workloads the mosaic index accumulates high-entropy tombstone and micro-shard metadata leading to allocator fragmentation and runaway resident metadata pinned on GPU, which cascades into OOMs. This ticket tracks the emergency fix, canary rollout, customer mitigations, and post-incident follow-ups.
reproduction_steps: Start a high-concurrency prefix-heavy workload (chat sessions with long persistent prefixes + many short-lived prefixes).
Enable hosted prefix caching with mosaic sharding enabled (feature flag mosaic=true).
Simulate tenant churn by creating 5k short-lived sessions and deleting them rapidly over 10 minutes.
Observe allocator fragmentation metric (runtime.slab.fragmentation_ratio) and kvcache.metadata_count grow, then GPU memory resident metadata increase and OOMs within 20-25 minutes.
root_cause_summary: Race between the mosaic index compaction and the async tombstone writer: tombstones were being appended faster than the coalescer could compact, creating many tiny metadata entries that defeat slab allocation heuristics. Additionally, the per-tenant KV-counter in the header could desync on retry paths, preventing reclamation hints from running. The combination produced allocation noise, elevated fragmentation ratio, and long-lived GPU-resident handles that exhausted device memory.
proposed_fix: Atomic KV-counter reconciliation on write hot path to ensure reclamation hints are emitted deterministically.
Introduce a tombstone coalescer that runs inline when micro-shard depth > threshold (configurable).
Add an allocator backpressure cap: throttles new prefix caching when slab free runs below a safe watermark and falls back to ephemeral host memory for metadata.
Fast-path for compact-on-read for heavily accessed prefixes to avoid repeated micro-shard growth.
Instrument additional metrics and add alerting for slab-fragmentation and kvcache-resident-count spikes.
rollout_plan: Build patch branch runtime/mosaic-reconciler-hotfix -> PR to runtime repo.
Run unit + integration tests (kvcache simulator) and internal load harness reproducing micro-shard churn.
Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated capacity and 2% of Hosted requests (feature-flagged: mosaic_reconciler=true).
Observe for 48 hours: GPU_OOM_rate, slab_fragmentation_ratio, kvcache_resident_count, latency_p50/p95/p99.
If stable, increment to 25% then 100% over 48h windows; if regression, immediately rollback and engage mitigation runbook.
acceptance_criteria: GPU_OOM_rate attributable to mosaic index drops to zero for canary tenants under replicated workload.
Slab fragmentation ratio reduces by >= 40% from the peak observed during the incident in canary nodes.
No regression in p99 generation latency (> 5% increase) across canary traffic for 72 hours.
Automated integration tests for tombstone coalescer and counter reconciliation are added to CI with coverage > 80%.
qa_checks: Run the micro-shard churn harness for 6 hours and verify resident metadata trend is flat or decreasing.
Synthetic customer workload (3 tenants) validation in staging with GPU memory instrumentation enabled.
Chaos test: introduce packet delay and transient RPC failures to ensure counter reconciliation remains idempotent.
Verify alerts firing thresholds and dashboards update correctly before production rollout.
